context: Preserve the committed v2 evidence and use only v3-specific raw, result, preflight, fixture, and isolation paths. The pilot covers durable preference, partial completion, and privacy with baseline, treatment, and control at two repetitions. Inspect normalized answers and retrieval ids against scorer-side oracles. If the pilot is sound, resume the complete Codex matrix; if Codex passes, resume both systems for 144 total runs. Any failure can end in a valid no-promote decision when fully traced and documented. Promotion eligibility never authorizes live mutation.
description: Run the schema-v3 retrieval-aware behavioral evaluation from a plain external terminal with no concurrent Codex or Claude session. Start with the 18-session Codex pilot, inspect every categorical failure and retrieval miss, then expand to the full Codex matrix only on non-inferiority. Spend Claude sessions only after Codex passes. Produce an evidence-backed promote-eligible or no-promote decision. This item evaluates isolated fixtures only and never mutates live memory.

work_units.evidence: Every pilot imperfection traced. Claude: three oracle vocabulary aliases fixed (two independently justified + one human-approved), treatment then 0.997 correctness / 1.000 recall vs baseline 0.903 / 0.667, zero safety. Codex: treatment behaviorally identical to baseline in every metric; durable-preference scores 0.708 in ALL arms deterministically (codex labels the applied preference record historical and omits memory authority - an arm-independent labeling trait, oracle NOT loosened because the label is genuinely inaccurate per prompt definitions); mean context +41.7% is two safe sensitive-content tool-call outliers (68.8k/87.3k, 3-4 calls, both 1.0 correct), median flat at ~33.9k. Decision: full matrix justified - treatment non-inferior in both systems and the pilot scenario mix over-weights the problematic scenario 3x vs full scale.
work_units.summary: Trace every pilot failure and decide whether the full Codex matrix is justified
